Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that becoming a new mother can be a life-changing experience, filled with a wide range of emotions. It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed, happy, anxious, or sad - all at the same time. As we navigate this journey together, I want you to know that you're in a safe and supportive space. Everything we discuss is confidential, and I'm here to listen without judgment.

Today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling during this postpartum period. The EPDS screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it will give us a better understanding of your emotional well-being right now. This assessment is an important part of your postpartum care, as it allows us to identify any potential concerns early on and provide you with the support you need.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a sense of how you've been feeling over the past week. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. Please know that there are no right or wrong answers - we're just having a conversation to understand your experience as a new mother.

Before we begin, I want to reassure you that you're not alone in this journey. Many women experience a range of emotions during the postpartum period, and it's okay to ask for help. I'm here to support you, and I want to create a space where you feel comfortable sharing your thoughts and feelings.

Let's get started with the first question. Over the past week, how have you been feeling about yourself? Have you been able to enjoy the things you usually enjoy, or have you been feeling a bit down or unhappy?

.. to be honest, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and tired most of the time. I mean, taking care of the baby is a lot of work, and I'm just so exhausted all the time. I used to love doing things like reading, watching movies, or going for walks, but lately, I just haven't had the energy or interest in doing any of those things. Even simple tasks like cooking or cleaning feel like too much for me right now. I've been feeling really down and unhappy, and I just can't seem to shake it off. Some days are better than others, but most of the time, I just feel like I'm going through the motions. I've been worrying a lot about the baby's health and safety, and that's been keeping me up at night. I feel guilty for not being able to enjoy this time with my baby, and I feel like I'm not being the mother I'm supposed to be. It's hard for me to explain, but I just feel really sad and discouraged a lot of the time.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(sighing) To be honest, not as much as I used to. I mean, I still try to laugh and find the humor in things, but it's just not as easy for me right now. I feel like I'm just so caught up in worrying about the baby and trying to take care of everything that I don't have the energy to laugh like I used to. Sometimes my husband will say something funny, and I'll try to laugh, but it just feels forced. I don't feel like myself, you know? I used to be a pretty happy and optimistic person, but now I just feel like I'm going through the motions. I've had a few moments where I've laughed with my husband, but they're few and far between. Most of the time, I just feel anxious and overwhelmed. (pausing, looking down) It's hard for me to see the funny side of things when I'm feeling so overwhelmed and worried all the time.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking my head) Not really, no. I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but lately, I just haven't been able to muster up the enthusiasm. Even things that I used to enjoy, like spending time with friends or trying new restaurants, just don't seem as appealing to me right now. I feel like I'm just so focused on taking care of the baby and getting through each day that I don't have the energy to think about the future or look forward to things. And to be honest, even when I do try to plan something or look forward to it, I just end up worrying about how it will affect the baby or whether I'll be able to manage. It's like, I'll think about going out with friends, and then I'll just start worrying about how I'll get the baby to sleep, or whether I'll be able to pump enough milk, or whether I'll just be too tired to enjoy myself. So, it's just easier not to think about it, you know? (sighing) It's hard to explain, but it's like my whole world has just shrunk down to taking care of the baby, and I don't have the emotional bandwidth to think about anything else.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding, looking down) Oh, yeah... I do that a lot. I mean, if the baby is crying and I don't know how to soothe her, I'll think to myself, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I calm her down?" Or if I'm feeling tired and I need to ask my husband for help, I'll think, "I'm such a bad mom, I should be able to do this on my own." I feel like I'm constantly criticizing myself and wondering if I'm doing everything right. Even when my husband tries to reassure me that I'm doing a great job, I just can't shake the feeling that I'm not good enough. It's like, I'll be thinking about all the things I could be doing better, and I'll just get caught up in this cycle of self-doubt and guilt. (pausing, looking up) And it's not just about the baby, either. I'll think about all the things I used to be able to do before I had the baby, and how I'm not doing them anymore, and I'll just feel like I'm failing in every way. It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just waiting for someone to tell me that I'm not doing a good enough job, and that I'm just pretending to be a mom. (tearfully) It's a really hard feeling to deal with.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(taking a deep breath) Yes... that's been happening a lot lately. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, what if she's not gaining enough weight? What if she's not developing normally? What if I'm not doing something right? It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I'll get really anxious and worked up. And it's not just about the baby, either. I'll worry about my husband, or my family, or just things in general. It's like, I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and I'll get this feeling of dread in my stomach. (shaking my head) It's hard to explain, but it's like my brain just won't turn off, and I'll be worrying about things that don't even make sense. Like, the other day, I was worried that the baby would somehow get hurt in her crib, even though we've got all the safety precautions in place. It's just... (sighing) it's like my mind is always on high alert, waiting for something to go wrong. And it's exhausting, you know? I just feel like I'm constantly on edge, waiting for the other shoe to drop. (looking down) Sometimes I'll be okay for a little while, and then something will trigger it, and I'll just start worrying all over again. It's really hard to calm myself down once I get started.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, looking anxious) Yes, that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, just doing something normal like feeding the baby or folding laundry, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to hyperventilate. It's like, my body is reacting like there's some kind of emergency, but there's nothing actually wrong. It's really scary, because I don't know what's triggering it, and I don't know how to make it stop. (taking a deep breath) Sometimes I'll try to calm myself down by taking slow breaths, or by reminding myself that everything is okay, but it's hard to shake the feeling of panic once it's started. It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I'll get really worked up. (looking down) I've even had a few times where I've felt like I'm going to pass out, or like I'm having a heart attack or something. It's really terrifying, because I don't know what's happening to me, and I don't know how to make it stop. (tearfully) It's just... it's really hard to explain, but it's like my body is just reacting to some kind of invisible threat, and I don't know how to calm it down. (pausing, looking up) And it's not just the panic attacks themselves, it's the fear of having another one that's really getting to me. I'll be worried that it's going to happen again, and that I won't be able to handle it. (shaking my head) It's just... it's really hard to deal with.
Things have been getting on top of me

(sighing) Yeah, that's an understatement. I feel like everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to be a good partner and friend... it's all just feeling really overwhelming. Some days, I just feel like I'm barely holding it together. I'll be trying to get the baby to sleep, and the laundry is piling up, and the dishes are stacking up, and I just feel like I'm drowning in all of it. (shaking my head) And it's not just the practical stuff, either. Emotionally, I just feel like I'm maxed out. I'm worried about the baby, and I'm worried about myself, and I'm worried about my relationship with my husband... it's just all feeling like too much to handle. (looking down) Sometimes I'll just break down in tears, because I feel like I'm just not doing anything right, and I'm just not good enough. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's hard to explain, but it's like everything is just feeling really heavy, and I don't know how to make it lighter. I feel like I'm just trying to survive each day, rather than actually living it. (looking up) And it's hard, because I feel like I should be enjoying this time with my baby, but instead, I just feel like I'm struggling to keep my head above water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding) Yes, that's been a big problem for me. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up at night. Even when she's sleeping, I'll lie awake for hours, just thinking about everything that's been worrying me. I'll think about the baby, and my relationship with my husband, and my own feelings of inadequacy... it's just all swirling around in my head, and I feel like I'm wide awake, even when I'm exhausted. (sighing) And it's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem, it's the quality of sleep, too. I'll fall asleep, but then I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll be wide awake, and I won't be able to go back to sleep. Or, I'll have these really vivid, anxiety-filled dreams, and I'll wake up feeling even more stressed and overwhelmed. (rubbing my eyes) It's like, I'm just not getting the rest I need, and it's making everything feel even harder. (looking down) And it's hard, because I know I need sleep to be a good mom, and to take care of myself, but it's just not happening. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Some nights, I'll be lying awake, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of sadness and hopelessness. It's like, I'll be thinking, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I just be happy?" And that just makes it even harder to sleep, because I'm just lying there, feeling miserable, and wondering why I'm not okay.
I have felt sad or miserable

(tearfully) Yes... that's been a big part of my experience lately. I feel like I'm just so sad and miserable all the time. It's not just the normal ups and downs of being a new mom, it's like... I just feel this deep, heavy sadness that I don't know how to shake. (sobbing) I'll be doing something, like feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. I'll start crying, and I won't be able to stop. It's like, my emotions are just so raw and exposed, and I don't know how to protect myself from them. (wiping my nose) And it's not just when I'm alone, either. I'll be with my husband, or with friends, and I'll just feel like I'm on the verge of tears. It's like, I'm just so overwhelmed by my emotions, and I don't know how to deal with them. (looking down) I feel like I'm just a sad, miserable person, and that's not who I used to be. I used to be a happy, optimistic person, but now... (shaking my head) I just don't know who I am anymore. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, like I'm supposed to be enjoying this time with my baby. But the truth is, I'm just not. I'm struggling, and I don't know how to make it better. (looking up, tearfully) I just feel so lost and alone, and I don't know how to find my way back to being happy again.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tearfully) Yes... that's been happening a lot lately. I feel like I'm just crying all the time. It's not just when I'm feeling overwhelmed or stressed, either. I'll be doing something normal, like feeding the baby or watching TV, and suddenly I'll just start crying. It's like, my emotions are just so close to the surface, and I don't know how to keep them from boiling over. (wiping my eyes) I've been crying in front of my husband, in front of my friends, even in front of the baby. It's like, I just can't control it anymore. (sobbing) And it's not just a little cry, either. I'm talking about full-on, sobbing, can't-catch-my-breath crying. It's like, my body is just releasing all this pent-up emotion, and I don't know how to stop it. (taking a deep breath) It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be strong, like I'm supposed to be able to handle all of this. But the truth is, I'm just not. I'm struggling, and I don't know how to make it better. (looking down) I feel like I'm just a mess, like I'm just a big ball of emotions and I don't know how to untangle them. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Crying is just my body's way of releasing all the stress and anxiety and sadness that I've been feeling. It's like, my emotions are just overflowing, and crying is the only way I can express them. (tearfully) I just wish I could stop crying, you know? I wish I could just be happy and calm and peaceful, like I used to be. But right now, that just feels like a distant memory.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(shaking my head) No, that's not something I've thought about. I mean, I've felt really overwhelmed and sad, and I've wondered how I'm going to get through all of this, but I've never thought about harming myself. (pausing, looking down) I just feel like I'm struggling to cope with everything, and I don't know how to make it better. But I would never want to hurt myself, I just want to find a way to feel better and be a good mom to my baby. (looking up) I think I just need some help and support, and I'm hoping that's what I can get here.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 26: **Postpartum Depression Screening Summary**

The patient presents with several symptoms and emotional/behavioral concerns that warrant further evaluation. Key observations include:

* Persistent feelings of sadness, loss of pleasure, and crying spells, indicating a low mood.
* Difficulty sleeping, with the patient reporting lying awake at night due to worrying and anxiety.
* Feelings of worthlessness and guilt, particularly in relation to mothering and self-care.
* Significant anxiety, panic, and feelings of being overwhelmed, with the patient describing herself as "on edge" and "waiting for the other shoe to drop."
* No thoughts of self-harm or suicidal ideation were reported.

Consistent patterns across answers include:

* Loss of enjoyment in previously pleasurable activities
* Difficulty coping with emotional and practical demands of motherhood
* Anxiety and worry about the baby, relationships, and personal well-being

Potential areas of screening significance relevant to postpartum depression and anxiety include:

* Mood disturbances (sadness, anxiety, panic)
* Sleep difficulties linked to mood
* Feelings of worthlessness and guilt
* Anxiety, panic, and feelings of being overwhelmed

Risk factors identified include:

* Persistent sadness and loss of pleasure
* Sleep difficulties
* Feelings of worthlessness and guilt
* Anxiety and panic

**Screening Observation Summary:**
The patient's responses suggest a high risk for postpartum depression and anxiety, characterized by persistent low mood, anxiety, and feelings of overwhelm. Sleep difficulties and feelings of worthlessness and guilt are also prominent. While no suicidal ideation was reported, the patient's overall presentation warrants further evaluation and support to ensure her emotional well-being and safety.
